title: Area-code-hunt shard B pass — NPAs 415, 424, 430

data.research_question: Which public organizations relevant to the anarchist-violence organization-enumeration corpus are discoverable from the next unresolved authoritative shard-B U.S. geographic NPAs 415, 424 and 430?
data.method: Bounded area-code organization enumeration using current NANPA geographic-area-code admission before deterministic NPA mod 3 sharding; literal anarchist, anarchist collective, Anarchist Black Cross, Food Not Bombs and mutual-aid queries; locality-derived searches; first-party organization pages; public social/resource hubs; public Reddit discovery without official APIs; historical directories only as discovery seeds; and repository exact-name search before canonical-ID creation.
classification_rules: Do not infer individual political affiliation from organization proximity or event participation.
Do not label an organization anarchist absent explicit organization-level evidence.
Historical directories and old social endpoints are discovery seeds until current status is corroborated.
Do not merge identities from name or handle similarity alone.
Completed NPAs are not repeated without materially new evidence.
A zero-hit code remains a zero-hit control instead of being padded with generic charities or ideologically unrelated organizations.

findings.notes: San Francisco produced Bound Together as a current explicit anarchist collective, current SF Food Not Bombs, and current SF Bay Area Mutual Aid.
Westside Los Angeles produced current Nourish LA with a public 424 contact and recurring 2026 food distributions; We Stay Here is retained as a 2025 mutual-aid project with current status unresolved.

Tyler, Longview and surrounding East Texas literal/locality searches did not produce a sufficiently evidence-backed anarchist, ABC/ABCF, Food Not Bombs or mutual-aid organization for materialization; generic charities and civic-service providers were excluded.
